title: Set up binference
disclaimer.wrongPhrase: Type {phrase} to accept, or press Ctrl+C to stop setting up.
disclaimer.accepted: You accepted the disclaimer. Going live does not ask for it again.
disclaimer.unread: Nobody is at a terminal to read the disclaimer, so `binference live` shows it before any agent goes live. To accept it during init, run it with --accept-disclaimer, which prints it in full first.
disclaimer.acceptedPrinted: You accepted the disclaimer and the privacy statement printed above. Going live does not ask for them again.
telemetry.ask: Share anonymous usage counts with the binference team?
telemetry.none: binference sends no usage counts yet. Your choice is kept in config.json5 and applies once it does.
model.title: Your model
model.explain: Your agent thinks with an AI model from a provider you pick: the bInference Router, OpenAI, Anthropic, OpenRouter, or any other provider of the OpenAI or Anthropic API, local models included. binference checks your key with one small call before it keeps the key. The call costs a fraction of a cent.
model.provider.openai-compatible: Another provider of the OpenAI API
model.provider.anthropic-compatible: Another provider of the Anthropic API
model.hint.openai-compatible: The OpenAI API at an address you type
model.hint.anthropic-compatible: The Anthropic API at an address you type
model.badBaseUrl: Type an address that starts with https://, or with http:// for a provider on this machine.
model.name: Model ID, as your provider writes it
model.badName: Type the model's ID without spaces.
model.keyOptional: API key (hidden as you type). Press Enter if your provider takes none
model.keyKept: API key (hidden as you type). Press Enter to keep the key binference holds
model.checking: Checking {model} at {provider} with one small call...
model.bad_key: {provider} did not accept this API key. Copy it again from your provider's dashboard.
model.no_credit: {provider} accepted the API key, but its account has no credit left or reached its spending limit. Add credit, then try again.
model.rate_limited: {provider} asked binference to slow down. Wait a minute, then try again.
model.unknown_model: {provider} does not know the model {model}. Check its exact ID in your provider's model list.
model.unreachable: No answer came from {address}, or it answered with a server error. Check the address and your network, then try again.
model.rejected: {address} did not take the call as a model API. Check the address, the model ID and which API the provider speaks.
service.ask: Start binference now as the background service? It then starts at each login.
service.homeMoved: BINFERENCE_HOME moves the state folder, so binference does not run as the background service. Start it with `binference start --foreground`.
privy.title: Your Privy app
privy.steps:
binference keeps every agent wallet in your own Privy app. To make one:
1. Create an account at https://dashboard.privy.io, then create an app.
2. Open Configuration, then App settings, then Basics.
3. Copy the app ID and the app secret, then paste each one below.
privy.appSecret: Privy app secret (hidden as you type)
privy.badAppId: A Privy app ID is letters and digits, as App settings shows it.
privy.checked: Privy accepted the app ID and the app secret.
privy.rejected: Privy did not accept this app ID and app secret. Copy both again from App settings.
ownerKey.title: Your owner key
ownerKey.checkBack: Type the last 6 characters of your owner key
ownerKey.checkWrong: That is not how your owner key ends. Check what you wrote down. {left, plural, =0 {No tries left.} one {# try left.} other {# tries left.}}
ownerKey.checked: You wrote down your owner key.
rescue.title: Your rescue address
rescue.explain: A rescue moves everything your agent wallets hold to your rescue address, in one tap, even while the agent is frozen. Use a wallet only you control, such as a hardware wallet.
rescue.invalid: This is no address on BNB Chain. Paste one that starts with 0x and has 40 more characters.
bot.title: Your Telegram bot
bot.steps: binference talks to you through a Telegram bot of your own. In Telegram, start a chat with @BotFather, type /newbot, and paste the bot token it gives you below.
bot.checked: Telegram accepted the bot token of @{username}.
bot.rejected: Telegram did not accept this bot token. Copy it again from @BotFather.
bot.malformed: This is no bot token. @BotFather writes one as digits, a colon, then letters and digits.
limits.title: Your agent's limits
limits.explain: Every trade stays inside these caps. You can lower them at any time, and raise them from the CLI or the console.
limits.invalid: Type an amount in US dollars, such as 100 or 0.5.
passphrase.ask: Passphrase for the agent key on this machine (hidden)
passphrase.mismatch: The two passphrases differ. Type the same passphrase twice.
wallet.making: Making your agent wallet on Privy, with its ceiling...
wallet.made: Privy holds your agent wallet {address}. Its owner, its signer and its ceiling are exactly what binference asked for.
done.title: binference is set up
done.wallet: Agent wallet: {address}. Fund it with BNB on BNB Chain when you go live.
done.paper: Your agent starts in paper mode and asks you before every trade: manual approval mode.
done.model: Model: {model} at {provider}. {place, select, keychain {Its API key is in the OS keychain.} file {Its API key is in an owner-only file in the keys folder.} source {binference reads its API key from the secret source you gave.} other {It takes no API key.}}
done.noModel: No model is linked yet, so the agent cannot chat. Run `binference init --start-over` in a terminal to link one.
done.goLive: To trade with real money, fund the wallet, then run `binference live` on this machine.{disclaimer, select, accepted { It does not ask for the disclaimer again.} other { It shows the disclaimer first.}}
done.nextService: Next: open the link above in Telegram once binference runs.
done.unlockMade: binference made this machine's agent key and keeps it {mode, select, keychain {in the OS keychain} file {in an owner-only file in the keys folder} manual {in the keys folder, sealed with your passphrase; run `binference unlock` after each start} other {in your secret manager}}.
done.unlockKept: This machine held an agent key already: binference keeps it {mode, select, keychain {in the OS keychain} file {in an owner-only file in the keys folder} manual {in the keys folder, sealed with your passphrase; run `binference unlock` after each start} other {in your secret manager}} and uses it.
done.pairing:
Start binference with `binference start`, then open this link in Telegram before {expires}. Whoever opens it first becomes the owner of @{bot}:
{link}
attach.appSecret: Privy app secret (hidden). This machine does not hold it yet where config.json5 names it; binference keeps it there
attach.botToken: Telegram bot token (hidden). This machine does not hold it yet where config.json5 names it; binference keeps it there
attach.sourcesMoved: config.json5 named {count, plural, one {# secret} other {# secrets}} in the old machine's keys folder; binference now reads {count, plural, one {it} other {them}} from this folder's keys folder.
attach.ownerKeyWrong: That is not the owner key of this install. Try again.
restore.ownerKey: Owner key code that opens the backup (hidden)
restore.ownerKeyWrong: That owner key does not open this backup. Try again.
restore.unknown: This install has no record of writing this file. Anyone who knows the owner key's public half can make a file that opens with the owner key, so restore it only if you know where it came from.
restore.unrecorded: This machine holds no record of the backups the install wrote, so check that this is your backup: its install, its time and its wallets.
restore.genuine: Type {day} if this is your backup. Anything else stops here and changes nothing
restore.placedAside: Restored the backup taken {when}. The state it replaced waits in {folder} for 7 days.
restore.undone: The restore is undone: the state folder is as it was before.
restore.startFailedUndone: binference did not start on the restored state, so the restore is undone: the state folder is as it was before, and binference starts again on it.
refused.restoreMoveFailed: The restored files could not be put in place in {folder}, so nothing changed: every file moved back. Run `binference logs` to see why, then restore again.
refused.restoreMixed: The restore stopped part way and could not move every file back, so {folder} holds parts of both states and binference stays stopped. The state it replaced waits in {aside}, the restored files in {staged}: move the files of {aside} back into {folder}, then start binference.
refused.restoreNotConfirmed: You did not type {day}, so nothing changed.
refused.restoreReplacedOlder: The engine database in this folder is from an older binference, so nothing changed. Start binference once so it updates the database, then restore again.
refused.restoreCarryFailed: The state in {folder} changed while binference stopped, so the restore could not keep its revokes and freezes, and nothing changed. Restore again.
restore.startService: Starting binference again as the background service.
restore.startHere: binference ran in a terminal, so it starts again here, in this terminal. Stop it with Ctrl+C.
restore.startYourself: binference was not running, so it stays stopped. Start it with `binference start`.
restore.changes.title: What this restore changes
restore.changes.kept: Kept as they are now: revoked devices and client tokens, the Telegram owner, every freeze, the rescue address and its pending change, and the spending of the last 24 hours.
restore.changes.history: History after the backup ({since}), up to {last}, leaves with the state this restore replaces, which waits 7 days in the replaced folder.
restore.changes.historyNone: Nothing happened after the backup ({since}), so no history is lost.
restore.changes.agentGone: Agent {name} was made after the backup and goes.
restore.changes.agentBack: Agent {name} comes back as the backup holds it.
restore.changes.walletGone: Wallet {label} ({address}) was added after the backup and leaves binference. Nothing in it moves.
restore.changes.frozen: The backup holds binference frozen, so it stays frozen after the restore.
restore.changes.guard: {guard, select, frozen {frozen} archived {archived} paper {paper mode} manual {manual mode} sendLevel {send level} other {a setting}}
restore.changes.stricter: Agent {agent} keeps the backup's stricter settings: {items}.
restore.changes.unreadable: The state this restore replaces cannot be read, so revokes, freezes and spending since the backup cannot be kept. Revoke devices and client tokens again after the restore.
restore.confirm: Type {day} to restore the backup taken {when}. Anything else stops here and changes nothing
refused.restoreNeedsAttach: --restore restores a backup as this machine attaches: run `binference init --attach --restore` with the backup file.
refused.restoreNotFound: There is no backup file at {file}.
refused.restoreNewerFormat: {file} was written by a newer binference. Update binference, then restore it.
refused.restoreOwnerKey: The owner key you typed does not open this backup, so nothing changed. A backup opens only with the owner key of the install it holds.
refused.restoreDamaged: {file} is damaged: a part of it does not match what was written, so nothing changed. Restore another backup.
refused.restoreNewerSchema: This backup holds data of a newer binference, so nothing changed. Update binference, then restore it.
refused.restoreWalletsDiffer: The wallets in this backup are not the ones Privy holds for this owner key, so nothing was restored. Restore a newer backup, or run `binference init --attach` on an empty folder to rebuild the install from Privy.
refused.restoreTerminal: binference backup restore asks for the owner key. Run it in a terminal, without --yes or --json.
refused.restoreConfig: config.json5 in {folder} does not load, so nothing changed. Run `binference check` to see the fix, then restore again.
refused.restoreOtherApp: This backup holds an install of another Privy app ({appId}) than config.json5 names, so nothing changed. Restore a backup of this install.
refused.restoreOtherSigner: The wallets list another signer than the one in this backup, so nothing changed: restoring it here would leave binference unable to sign. Run `binference stop`, then `binference init --attach --restore` with the backup file: it restores the backup and makes this machine the wallets' signer.
refused.restoreStopLate: binference did not stop on {folder} in time, so nothing changed. Run `binference logs` to see why, then restore again.
refused.restoreEngineStarted: binference started again on {folder} before the backup was put in place, so nothing changed. Run `binference stop`, then restore again.
attach.moving: Making this machine the signer of {count, plural, one {# wallet} other {# wallets}} on Privy, with the owner key.
attach.done.title: This machine signs for the wallets
attach.done.wallets: This machine now signs for {count, plural, one {# wallet} other {# wallets}}. Its signer ID is {signer}.
attach.done.removed: Removed signer {signers} from every wallet: the machine that held it signs nothing more.
attach.done.noBot: binference cannot read the bot token where `telegram.botToken` names it, so it starts without the Telegram bot. Put the token back there, then run `binference restart`.
attach.done.next: Next: on the old machine, run `binference service remove`, so it stops and no longer starts at login: two machines cannot poll one Telegram bot. Then run `binference start` here, and `binference telegram pair` to pair the bot with this machine.
rebuild.title: Rebuild from Privy
rebuild.warning: This folder holds no install. binference rebuilds what Privy holds: the wallets your owner key owns, their ceilings, and the rescue address when the ceilings show it. Everything else starts fresh: trade history, orders, positions, settings and limits, wallet labels, saved addresses and the Telegram pairing. Rebuild only when the old machine and its state folder are gone; to move from a machine that still runs, copy its stopped state folder without keys/ instead.
rebuild.noWallets: Privy's app holds no wallet this owner key owns. Check the code and try again.
rebuild.found:
Privy holds {count, plural, one {# wallet} other {# wallets}} your owner key owns. Check that you made each one:
{wallets}
rebuild.foundWallet: {address}, made {made}{role, select, launch {, a launch wallet} other {}}
rebuild.extraLaunch: Your owner key owns more than one launch wallet. The newest, {address}, becomes the agent's launch wallet. Nothing trades from the {count, plural, one {other one} other {# others}}: once binference runs, rescue what {count, plural, one {it holds} other {they hold}} with `binference rescue`.
rebuild.rescueRead: The rescue address is {address}: the one address every ceiling lets a send pay.
rebuild.rescueAsk: Rescue address: one of the addresses every ceiling lets a send pay, {addresses}
rebuild.rescueNotListed: That is not an address every ceiling lets a send pay.
rebuild.confirm: Type {count} to rebuild {count, plural, one {this wallet} other {these wallets}} on this machine, with a fresh history
rebuild.done.title: binference is rebuilt on this machine
rebuild.done.wallets: This machine now signs for {count, plural, one {# wallet} other {# wallets}}: {addresses}. Its signer ID is {signer}. The rescue address is {rescue}.
rebuild.done.fresh: History, orders, settings, wallet labels and saved addresses start fresh. Saved addresses stay in the ceilings: run `binference address add` with the owner key to send to one again.
refused.alreadySetUp: binference is set up in {folder} already. To set it up again with a new owner key and a new wallet, run `binference init --start-over`.
refused.engineRunning: binference is running on {folder}. Stop it, then run `binference init`.
refused.storeDamaged: The database {file} failed its integrity check. Restore a backup, then run `binference init` again.
refused.needsAnswer: binference init needs {flag}. Give that flag, set {variable}, or write {key} in the answers file.
refused.secretInline: {name} holds a secret as plain text. binference init takes a secret only as a secret source that says where it is kept, such as {example}, or with `fromFile`, `fromKeychain` or `fromCommand`. If that text was a real secret, replace it where it was issued.
refused.unknownVariable: {variable} answers nothing binference init asks. Remove it, or fix its name: each BINFERENCE_INIT_ variable is a flag of `binference init --help` in capitals, such as BINFERENCE_INIT_PRIVY_APP_ID.
refused.answersMissing: There is no answers file at {file}. Check the path that `--answers` or `BINFERENCE_INIT_ANSWERS` gives.
refused.answersUnreadable: The answers file {file} cannot be read at line {line}, column {column}. Fix it there, then run `binference init` again.
refused.answersNotObject: The answers file {file} must hold one JSON5 object, with one entry for each answer.
refused.answersInvalid: The answers file {file} holds something binference init does not take at {key}. Each entry is named after a flag of `binference init --help` in camel case, such as `privyAppId`, and `set` holds config keys.
refused.badAnswer: {name} holds a value binference init does not take. Run `binference init --help` to see what it takes.
refused.badSource: {flag} is no secret source. Write it as config.json5 writes one, with fromEnv, fromFile, fromKeychain or fromCommand.
refused.sourceUnavailable: binference cannot read the secret that {flag} names: {reason, select, not_set {the variable is not set} not_found {nothing is there} empty {it is empty} timeout {the program printed nothing within 10 seconds} other {the program failed}}. Fix it, then run `binference init` again.
refused.badAppId: {flag} is no Privy app ID. Copy it from App settings in the Privy dashboard.
refused.privyRejected: Privy did not accept this app ID and app secret. Copy both again from App settings in the Privy dashboard.
refused.ownerKeyUnconfirmed: You did not confirm your owner key, so binference made nothing and the key is gone. Run `binference init` again for a new owner key.
refused.ownerKeyTerminal: binference init shows a new owner key once, in a terminal only, and nobody is at one here. Run it in a terminal without --yes or --json, or run `binference owner-key create` on a machine with a terminal and pass the public half it prints with --owner-key-public.
refused.ownerKeyPublic: --owner-key-public takes the public half `binference owner-key create` printed: a P-256 key in base64. Check what you passed and try again.
refused.attachOwnerKeyPublic: --attach and --owner-key-public cannot go together: attach asks for the owner key code itself.
refused.badRescue: {flag} is no address on BNB Chain. Give an address that starts with 0x and has 40 more characters.
refused.modelProvider: `--model-provider` names no provider init offers. Give one of: {providers}.
refused.modelAddress: `--model-base-url` takes an address that starts with https://, or with http:// for a provider on this machine.
refused.model.bad_key: {provider} did not accept the API key, so binference made nothing. Copy it again from your provider's dashboard, then run `binference init` again.
refused.model.no_credit: {provider} accepted the API key, but its account has no credit left or reached its spending limit, so binference made nothing. Add credit, then run `binference init` again.
refused.model.rate_limited: {provider} asked binference to slow down, so binference made nothing. Wait a few minutes, then run `binference init` again.
refused.model.unknown_model: {provider} does not know the model {model}, so binference made nothing. Check its exact ID in your provider's model list, then run `binference init` again.
refused.model.unreachable: No answer came from {address}, or it answered with a server error, so binference made nothing. Check the address and your network, then run `binference init` again.
refused.model.rejected: {address} did not take the call as a model API, so binference made nothing. Check the address, the model ID and which API the provider speaks, then run `binference init` again.
refused.bot.rejected: Telegram did not accept this bot token. Copy it again from @BotFather.
refused.bot.malformed: This is no bot token. Copy it again from @BotFather.
refused.manualNeedsTerminal: The manual unlock mode asks for a passphrase. Run `binference init` in a terminal, without --yes or --json.
refused.passphraseMismatch: The passphrases did not match, so binference made nothing. Run `binference init` again.
refused.agentKeyUnreadable: {flag} gave no agent key. It must print a P-256 private key as one line of base64 DER (PKCS #8).
refused.setOwned: binference init sets {path} itself. Leave out that --set flag.
refused.configInvalid: The settings init would write have {count, plural, one {# problem} other {# problems}}. Fix the --set flags, then run `binference init` again.
refused.unknownVenue: {venue} is no venue this binference installs. Remove it from `defaults.limits.venues`.
refused.unknownChain: {chain} is no chain this binference serves. Remove it from `chains.enabled`.
refused.badCeilingCap: `defaults.ceiling.perTxBnb` is {cap}, which BNB cannot hold. Give a decimal with at most 18 places.
refused.badGasReserve: `defaults.limits.gasReserve` names {chain}, which this binference does not serve, or an amount its coin cannot hold.
refused.badToken: {token} is no token on a chain this binference serves, as CAIP-19 writes it. Fix `defaults.limits.allowTokens` or `defaults.limits.denyTokens`.
refused.badCeiling: The ceiling cannot be built: {problem, select, too_many_addresses {it names more than 100 addresses} malformed_address {it names an address that is not valid} too_many_caps {it needs more 24-hour caps than the 10 Privy keeps for an app} other {its chains are not valid}}.
refused.readBack: Privy's new wallet is not what binference asked for: {problem, select, owner {its owner differs} signer {its signer differs} policy {its ceiling differs} not_found {Privy does not hold it} other {it is no Ethereum wallet}}. binference will not use it. Run `binference init --start-over` to make another.
refused.agentNameTaken: An agent named {name} exists already. Rename it, then run `binference init --start-over`.
refused.attachStartOver: --attach and --start-over cannot go together: attach keeps the install and its wallets, and a start over replaces them.
refused.attachConfig: config.json5 in {folder} does not load. Run `binference check` to see the fix, then run `binference init --attach` again.
refused.attachOtherApp: config.json5 names another Privy app than the one that holds this install's wallets. Set `custody.privy.appId` back to {appId}.
refused.attachNoAppSecret: config.json5 names no Privy app secret. Set `custody.privy.appSecret`, then run `binference init --attach` again.
refused.attachAppSecret: binference cannot read the Privy app secret where `custody.privy.appSecret` names it. Put it back there, then run `binference init --attach` again.
refused.attachOwnerKeyTerminal: binference init --attach asks for the owner key. Run it in a terminal, without --yes or --json.
refused.attachOwnerKey: That is not the owner key of this install, so nothing changed.
refused.attachedAlready: This machine holds the agent key that signs for the wallets already. Nothing changed.
refused.attachLeftOpen: {file} is still open: an engine ran on it when it was copied, or stopped without letting it go. On the old machine, run `binference service remove`, then copy the state folder again. On the machine that ran it, run `binference start`, then `binference stop`, and attach again.
refused.attachCopiedKeys: {folder} holds the agent key the wallets name now. If you copied it from the old machine, delete {folder} and run `binference init --attach` again: this machine needs a key of its own. If this machine signs for the wallets already, nothing needs attaching.
refused.attachMovedSource: config.json5 names {from} for `{path}`, in another machine's keys folder, written in a way binference does not change. Set it to {to}, then run `binference init --attach` again.
refused.attachConfigOnly: {folder} holds a config file but no install, so there is nothing to attach and nothing to rebuild over it. Move config.json5 away to rebuild from Privy, then run `binference init --attach` again.
refused.rebuildNoWallets: Privy's app holds no wallet this owner key owns, so nothing was rebuilt. Check the owner key code and the Privy app, then run `binference init --attach` again.
refused.rebuildOnlyLaunch: Your owner key owns only launch wallets, so nothing was rebuilt: an agent needs a wallet that is no launch wallet as its default. Run `binference init` on an empty folder to set up a new install; the launch wallets stay on Privy under your owner key.
refused.rebuildRescue: The rescue address must be one every ceiling lets a send pay: {addresses}. Give one of them with --rescue, or run `binference init --attach` in a terminal.
refused.rebuildNotConfirmed: You did not type the number of wallets, so nothing was rebuilt and nothing changed on Privy.
refused.attachRefused: Privy did not take the owner key's signature, so the wallets it did not reach keep their signer. Run `binference init --attach` again.
refused.attachExpired: A change reached Privy after its expiry, so the wallets after it still list the old signer. Run `binference init --attach` again; it goes on from where it stopped.
refused.attachQuorum: Privy holds this machine's new key quorum with other keys than its agent key, so no wallet moved. Run `binference init --attach` again.
refused.attachWalletGone: Privy no longer holds one of this install's wallets, so the wallets after it keep their signer. Check the wallets in the Privy dashboard.
fault.signersReadBack: Privy read a wallet back with another signer than this machine set. Run `binference init --attach` again; if Privy reads it back so again, check the wallet in the Privy dashboard.
fault.cancelled: binference init stopped. It made nothing on Privy.
fault.privyUnreachable: Privy did not respond. Check your network, then run `binference init` again.
fault.privyBusy: Privy asked binference to slow down. Wait a minute, then run `binference init` again.
fault.privyFailed: Privy refused a call ({code}). Run `binference init` again in a few minutes.
fault.telegramUnreachable: Telegram did not respond. Check your network, then run `binference init` again.
fault.telegramBusy: Telegram asked binference to wait. Wait a few minutes, then run `binference init` again.
fault.telegramFailed: Telegram refused a call ({code}). Run `binference init` again in a few minutes.
fault.keychain: The OS keychain did not respond. Unlock it, or run `binference init --unlock file`.
fault.passphraseRejected: This passphrase does not open the agent key this machine holds. Run `binference init` again with the passphrase you set before.
fault.agentKeyInvalid: The keys folder holds an agent key binference cannot read. Put back your copy of it, then run `binference init` again.
fault.agentKeyNotStored: The agent key did not stay where the unlock mode keeps it. Check that the keychain or the keys folder takes writes, then run `binference init` again.
fault.unexpected: binference init stopped on an error ({code}). Run `binference init` again; if it stops again, report the code.
